questions.stem: In a DNA molecule, adenine always pairs with
questions.explanation: Adenine pairs with thymine and guanine pairs with cytosine, a rule known as complementary base pairing. Because each base has only one partner, an unzipped strand specifies exactly what the new strand must be, which is how DNA copies itself accurately.

distractorRationale.a: Guanine is the partner of cytosine, not of adenine
distractorRationale.c: Cytosine pairs with guanine
distractorRationale.d: The two strands are complementary, not identical, so a base never pairs with its own kind

questions.stem: An organism whose two alleles of a gene are different, such as Tt, is described as
questions.explanation: Heterozygous means the two alleles at a locus differ. Such an organism shows the dominant phenotype but can pass on the recessive allele, which is why heterozygotes are often described as carriers.

distractorRationale.a: Homozygous dominant would be TT, with two identical dominant alleles
distractorRationale.d: Haploid refers to having one set of chromosomes, as in a gamete, not to the alleles present

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes genotype from phenotype?

options.text: Genotype is the visible characteristic; phenotype is the alleles present
Genotype is the alleles an organism carries; phenotype is the observable characteristic that results
They are two names for the same thing
Genotype applies to plants and phenotype to animals

questions.explanation: The genotype is the genetic instruction and the phenotype is the outcome you can observe. The distinction matters because different genotypes can give the same phenotype: TT and Tt peas are both tall, yet only the Tt plant can produce dwarf offspring.

distractorRationale.a: The two definitions have been swapped
distractorRationale.c: They are distinct: the same phenotype can arise from more than one genotype
distractorRationale.d: Both terms apply to all organisms

questions.stem: A maize root cell contains 20 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are present in the nucleus of one of its pollen grains?
questions.explanation: A root cell is a body cell, so 20 is the diploid number. Pollen carries the male gamete, formed by meiosis, which halves the number to the haploid 10. Fusion with a 10-chromosome egg cell then restores 20 in the zygote.

distractorRationale.a: This halves the number twice; meiosis halves it once overall
distractorRationale.c: This is the diploid body-cell number, which gametes do not have
distractorRationale.d: This doubles instead of halving

questions.stem: A gene may best be described as

options.text: a length of DNA that codes for one protein and so controls one characteristic
a single base in a DNA molecule
the protein produced by a cell

questions.explanation: A gene is a functional segment of a chromosome. Its sequence of bases, read three at a time, specifies the order of amino acids in a protein, and that protein in turn produces the characteristic we observe.

distractorRationale.a: One chromosome carries many hundreds or thousands of genes
distractorRationale.c: A single base is far too small to code for anything; three bases specify one amino acid
distractorRationale.d: The protein is the product of the gene, not the gene itself

questions.stem: Sickle cell anaemia is caused by a change in a single base of the gene for haemoglobin. Such a change is called a
questions.explanation: A gene mutation alters the base sequence within one gene, changing one amino acid in the protein it codes for. That single substitution makes haemoglobin S, which distorts red blood cells into a sickle shape when oxygen is low.

distractorRationale.b: A chromosomal mutation alters the number or structure of whole chromosomes, as in Down syndrome
distractorRationale.c: Crossing over exchanges segments between homologous chromosomes without altering base sequences
distractorRationale.d: Independent assortment reshuffles existing chromosomes during meiosis

questions.stem: One strand of a short length of DNA has the base sequence A-T-G-C-A. The complementary strand will read
questions.explanation: Apply the pairing rule base by base: A pairs with T, T with A, G with C, C with G and A with T, giving T-A-C-G-T. This is exactly the reasoning a cell uses when it replicates DNA, which is why copying is so reliable.

distractorRationale.a: This repeats the original strand instead of complementing it
distractorRationale.c: The bases have been rearranged rather than paired
distractorRationale.d: The pairing rule has been applied inconsistently across the sequence

questions.stem: Two organisms with the same phenotype must have the same genotype.
questions.explanation: False. A dominant allele masks a recessive one, so TT and Tt pea plants are both tall despite having different genotypes. This is why a test cross with a homozygous recessive individual is needed to reveal which genotype an organism actually has.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a mutagen — an agent that increases the rate of mutation?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays are ionising radiation with enough energy to break chemical bonds in DNA, altering base sequences or damaging whole chromosomes. Ultraviolet light, X-rays and certain chemicals, including those in tobacco smoke, act in the same way.

distractorRationale.a: Vitamin C is a nutrient and an antioxidant, not a mutagen
distractorRationale.c: Distilled water is chemically inert with respect to DNA
distractorRationale.d: Dietary fibre passes through the gut without entering cells

questions.stem: Define gene, allele, genotype, phenotype, dominant allele and recessive allele, giving one example for each. Explain why complementary base pairing in DNA makes accurate copying possible.
markingGuide: Gene: a length of DNA coding for one protein and hence one characteristic, with a valid example (1 mark)
Allele: one of the alternative forms of a gene, for example T for tall and t for dwarf (1 mark)
Genotype: the alleles an organism carries, for example Tt (1 mark)
Phenotype: the observable characteristic, for example tall (1 mark)
Dominant allele: expressed even when only one copy is present, written as a capital letter, for example T (2 marks)
Recessive allele: expressed only when two copies are present, written in lower case, for example t (2 marks)

Base pairing: adenine pairs only with thymine and guanine only with cytosine, so when the double helix unzips each exposed base specifies exactly one partner and each old strand acts as a template for a new one, producing two identical molecules (3 marks)
questions.explanation: Each definition must be paired with an example that actually illustrates it, since examiners award the example mark separately. The base pairing explanation should make clear that the strictness of the pairing rule is what removes ambiguity, so each parent strand determines its partner uniquely.

questions.stem: What is the basic structural unit of DNA?
questions.explanation: A nucleotide is the basic structural unit of DNA, consisting of a sugar, a phosphate group, and a nitrogenous base. These nucleotides link together to form the DNA strand, which carries genetic information.

distractorRationale.b: A chromosome is a structure that contains DNA and proteins, but it is not the basic unit of DNA itself.
distractorRationale.c: A gene is a segment of DNA that codes for a specific trait but is not the structural unit of DNA.
distractorRationale.d: An allele is a variant form of a gene, not a unit of DNA.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a dominant allele?

options.text: An allele that is expressed only in the homozygous condition
An allele that masks the effect of another allele
An allele that is always expressed in a phenotype
An allele that is recessive in nature

questions.explanation: A dominant allele is one that can mask the effect of another allele when present. In a heterozygous genotype, the dominant allele's trait will be expressed in the phenotype.

distractorRationale.a: This describes a recessive allele, which requires two copies to be expressed.
distractorRationale.c: While dominant alleles are often expressed, they are not always expressed in every situation.
distractorRationale.d: This is incorrect as a dominant allele is not recessive.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: How is chromosome number maintained during cell division?

options.text: Through the process of mitosis and meiosis
By the replication of DNA only

questions.explanation: Chromosome number is maintained through the processes of mitosis, which produces identical daughter cells, and meiosis, which reduces the chromosome number by half for gamete formation. This ensures that the chromosome number remains consistent across generations.

distractorRationale.b: DNA replication is part of the process but does not explain how chromosome number is maintained.
distractorRationale.c: Ribosomes are involved in protein synthesis, not chromosome maintenance.
distractorRationale.d: Transcription is the process of making RNA from DNA, not related to chromosome number.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: Which of the following terms refers to the physical expression of a genotype?
questions.explanation: Phenotype refers to the observable physical characteristics of an organism, which result from the interaction of its genotype with the environment. It is how the genetic makeup is expressed.

distractorRationale.a: Genotype refers to the genetic makeup, not the physical expression.
distractorRationale.c: An allele is a variant form of a gene, not the expression.
distractorRationale.d: Locus refers to the specific location of a gene on a chromosome.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: If a pea plant has a genotype of Tt, which of the following phenotypes could it exhibit?
questions.explanation: In pea plants, the allele for tall (T) is dominant over the allele for short (t). Therefore, a plant with a genotype of Tt will exhibit the tall phenotype due to the presence of the dominant allele.

distractorRationale.b: A short phenotype would only be expressed if the genotype were tt (homozygous recessive).
distractorRationale.c: Medium is not a recognized phenotype in this context.
distractorRationale.d: Variable is not a specific phenotype but rather indicates inconsistency.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about alleles?

options.text: They can be dominant or recessive
They are found only on sex chromosomes
They are not related to genes

questions.explanation: Alleles are different forms of a gene that can occupy the same locus on a chromosome. They can be classified as dominant or recessive depending on their effect on the phenotype.

distractorRationale.a: Alleles can be different; they do not have to be identical.
distractorRationale.c: Alleles can be found on any chromosome, not just sex chromosomes.
distractorRationale.d: Alleles are directly related to genes as they are variations of a specific gene.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: What is a homozygous genotype?

options.text: A genotype with two identical alleles
A genotype with two different alleles
A genotype that cannot express a phenotype

questions.explanation: A homozygous genotype consists of two identical alleles for a particular gene, such as TT or tt. This can lead to consistent expression of the associated phenotype.

distractorRationale.b: This describes a heterozygous genotype, which has different alleles.
distractorRationale.c: Genotypes typically involve two alleles for each gene.
distractorRationale.d: Homozygous genotypes can express phenotypes depending on the alleles present.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about chromosomes is correct?

options.text: Chromosomes are made up of RNA
Humans have 46 chromosomes in somatic cells
Chromosomes are only present during cell division
Each chromosome is made up of a single gene

questions.explanation: Humans have 46 chromosomes in their somatic (body) cells, organized into 23 pairs. This number is maintained through cell division processes.

distractorRationale.a: Chromosomes are primarily made up of DNA and proteins, not RNA.
distractorRationale.c: Chromosomes are present in the nucleus of cells even when the cell is not dividing, though they are in a less condensed form.
distractorRationale.d: Each chromosome can contain many genes, not just a single gene.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes a recessive allele?

options.text: An allele that is expressed only in the homozygous condition
An allele that can mask a dominant allele
An allele that is always expressed in a phenotype
An allele that is found only in females

questions.explanation: A recessive allele is only expressed in the phenotype when two copies are present (homozygous condition). In a heterozygous condition, it is masked by the presence of a dominant allele.

distractorRationale.b: This describes a dominant allele, which can mask the effect of a recessive allele.
distractorRationale.c: Recessive alleles are not expressed when a dominant allele is present.
distractorRationale.d: Alleles can be found in both males and females, not restricted to one sex.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: What is the relationship between DNA and genes?

options.text: DNA is made up of genes
Genes are segments of DNA that code for proteins
Genes are larger than DNA molecules

questions.explanation: Genes are specific sequences of nucleotides within DNA that provide the instructions for making proteins. Thus, genes are segments of DNA.

distractorRationale.a: DNA is composed of many genes, not the other way around.
distractorRationale.c: DNA and genes are directly related; genes are part of DNA.
distractorRationale.d: Genes are not larger than DNA molecules; they are segments within them.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: During which phase of cell division do chromosomes become visible?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes become visible during prophase, the first stage of mitosis, when the chromatin condenses and the nuclear envelope breaks down. This visibility is crucial for the proper alignment and separation of chromosomes.

distractorRationale.a: During interphase, chromosomes are in a less condensed form and not visible.
distractorRationale.c: While chromosomes are aligned during metaphase, they are not as clearly visible as in prophase.
distractorRationale.d: During telophase, chromosomes begin to de-condense again, making them less visible.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the structure of DNA?

options.text: A double helix made of nucleotides
A single strand of amino acids

questions.explanation: DNA is structured as a double helix, which consists of two strands of nucleotides twisted around each other. Each nucleotide contains a sugar, a phosphate group, and a nitrogenous base, which are crucial for genetic information storage.

distractorRationale.b: Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins, not DNA.
distractorRationale.c: DNA does not form a triple helix; it is primarily a double helix.
distractorRationale.d: Lipids are not components of DNA's structure.

questions.stem: What is the role of alleles in genetics?

options.text: They determine the physical traits of an organism.
They are responsible for the structure of DNA.
They are the same for all individuals of a species.
They are involved in the replication of DNA.

questions.explanation: Alleles are different forms of a gene that can produce variations in traits. They play a crucial role in determining the physical characteristics (phenotype) of an organism.

distractorRationale.b: The structure of DNA is determined by nucleotides, not alleles.
distractorRationale.c: Alleles can vary among individuals of the same species.
distractorRationale.d: DNA replication involves enzymes, not alleles.

questions.stem: If an organism has two identical alleles for a trait, it is said to be:
questions.explanation: An organism with two identical alleles for a trait is described as homozygous. This means both alleles are the same, whether dominant or recessive.

distractorRationale.a: Heterozygous refers to having different alleles.
distractorRationale.c: Dominant refers to an allele that can express its trait over a recessive one.
distractorRationale.d: Recessive refers to an allele that is masked by a dominant allele.

questions.stem: What is the significance of the chromosome number being maintained across generations?

options.text: It ensures stability of the species.

questions.explanation: Maintaining a consistent chromosome number across generations is crucial for the stability of a species. It ensures that offspring receive the correct amount of genetic material necessary for proper development.

distractorRationale.a: Genetic variation arises from mutations and recombination, not from chromosome number maintenance.
distractorRationale.c: While mutations can occur, maintaining chromosome number does not prevent them.
distractorRationale.d: Protein synthesis is a separate process from chromosome number maintenance.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about dominant and recessive alleles is correct?

options.text: A dominant allele can mask the expression of a recessive allele.
Recessive alleles are always expressed in the phenotype.
Dominant alleles are only found in homozygous genotypes.
Recessive alleles are never passed to offspring.

questions.explanation: A dominant allele is one that can mask the expression of a recessive allele in a heterozygous genotype. This means that the trait associated with the dominant allele will be expressed in the phenotype.

distractorRationale.b: Recessive alleles are expressed only when in a homozygous condition.
distractorRationale.c: Dominant alleles can be present in both homozygous and heterozygous genotypes.
distractorRationale.d: Recessive alleles can be passed to offspring even if they are not expressed in the parent's phenotype.

questions.stem: During which process does DNA replication occur?
questions.explanation: DNA replication occurs during the interphase of the cell cycle, specifically in the S phase, before a cell divides. This ensures that each daughter cell receives an identical set of chromosomes.

distractorRationale.a: Meiosis is a type of cell division that reduces chromosome number but does not directly involve DNA replication.
distractorRationale.b: Mitosis is the process of cell division, but DNA replication occurs beforehand during interphase.
distractorRationale.d: Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm, not related to DNA replication.

questions.stem: Which term describes the observable characteristics of an organism?
questions.explanation: Phenotype refers to the observable characteristics or traits of an organism, which result from the interaction of its genotype with the environment.

distractorRationale.a: Genotype refers to the genetic makeup of an organism, not its observable traits.
distractorRationale.c: An allele is a variant form of a gene, not a characteristic.
distractorRationale.d: Chromosomes are structures that carry genes but do not describe observable traits.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the relationship between genes and chromosomes?

options.text: Genes are segments of DNA located on chromosomes.
Chromosomes are made entirely of proteins.
Genes can exist independently of chromosomes.
Chromosomes do not contain genetic information.

questions.explanation: Genes are segments of DNA that are found on chromosomes, which serve as the carriers of genetic information. Each chromosome can contain many genes.

distractorRationale.b: Chromosomes are made of DNA and proteins, not entirely of proteins.
distractorRationale.c: Genes are always located on chromosomes within the cell nucleus.
distractorRationale.d: Chromosomes are essential for containing and transmitting genetic information.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of DNA in living organisms?

options.text: To provide energy for cellular activities.
To store and transmit genetic information.
To transport nutrients across cell membranes.

questions.explanation: The primary function of DNA is to store and transmit genetic information, which is essential for the growth, development, and reproduction of living organisms.

distractorRationale.a: Energy for cellular activities is derived from ATP, not DNA.
distractorRationale.c: Catalysis is mainly performed by enzymes, not DNA.
distractorRationale.d: Nutrient transport is a function of cell membranes and proteins, not DNA.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: What is an allele?

options.text: A variant form of a gene.
The physical location of a gene.
The complete set of genes in an organism.
A segment of DNA that does not code for a protein.

questions.explanation: An allele is a variant form of a gene that can result in different traits. For example, a gene for flower color may have a red allele and a white allele.

distractorRationale.b: The physical location of a gene is called a locus.
distractorRationale.c: The complete set of genes is referred to as the genome.
distractorRationale.d: Not all segments of DNA are considered alleles, especially if they do not code for functional traits.

questions.stem: Which of the following processes is responsible for the formation of gametes?
questions.explanation: Meiosis is the process of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half, resulting in the formation of gametes (sperm and eggs) with half the genetic material of the parent organism.

distractorRationale.a: Mitosis results in daughter cells that are genetically identical to the parent cell, not gametes.
distractorRationale.c: Fertilization is the fusion of gametes, not their formation.
distractorRationale.d: Binary fission is a form of asexual reproduction in some organisms, not related to gamete formation.
